 MISSOULA, Mont. — The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission has announced two product recalls involving mattresses and residential gas boilers because of fire and other safety hazards.
 About 50 Pamag Pieeoo twin XL mattresses are being recalled because they violate federal flammability standards, posing a risk of serious injury or death in a fire.
 The 8-inch mattresses were sold on Amazon.com in March 2026 for $80 to $95. They have white tops and sides with a gray curved pattern. The model number, BFC8HMBYTX-US, is printed on a label sewn into the side.
 Consumers should stop using the mattresses and contact Longjili Trading for a full refund. The company is asking customers to write "RECALLED" on the mattress, email a photo to Pamagpieeoo@outlook.com and dispose of the product.
 No injuries have been reported.
 In a separate recall, more than 4,700 NTI and HTP residential gas boilers are being recalled because of fire, carbon monoxide poisoning and impact hazards.
 The boilers were sold nationwide through heating and plumbing contractors and wholesale distributors from May 2021 through July 2026 for $3,200 to $7,700.
 The affected models include NTI's FTVN and TFTN series and HTP's EFTU series. Model and serial numbers are located on a rating plate on the left side of each boiler.
 According to the CPSC, a condensate dish inside the boiler can crack during delayed ignition, allowing gas to accumulate. If the gas ignites, the boiler's front cover could detach.
 The company has received 34 reports of the dish breaking, including three incidents involving detached covers. One technician reportedly suffered a broken jaw.
 Consumers should stop using the recalled boilers and contact Ariston to schedule a free repair by a certified technician. Those who must continue using their boilers while awaiting repairs should ensure working smoke and carbon monoxide alarms are installed.
 Ariston can be reached at 800-688-2575 or VCexchanger@ariston.com .
